title: PewDiePie Workout Review (5 Day Dumbbell Only Split)
summary: He reviews the 5-day dumbbell-only split PewDiePie appears to follow. He trims redundant press and lunge variations into rotations, widens rep ranges to 8-12, and swaps kickbacks for overhead extensions and supinated rows for safer options. He builds supersets throughout, adds forearm and trap volume, and spreads the five days over a 7-8 day window. Overall he rates it a good dumbbell program.
claims: A famous novice could easily sell workout programs to followers who would buy anything; he hopes PewDiePie avoids that trap
Dumbbell-only training is less efficient than barbells: you outgrow 100 lb dumbbells fast on deadlifts, and goblet or dumbbell squats are different movements from back squats
He trained with dumbbells only for years as a novice; it is fine at that stage, but learning barbell patterns early helps later progress
Chest and shoulders together is a high-synergy pairing and a good way to start the week
Do not do heavy barbell squats and deadlifts back to back on the same day
After a deadlift day, vertical pulls like pull-ups suit the next day: they hit the lats and decompress the spine and sacrum
Novices should usually have fewer but heavier lower-body days than upper-body days because the lower body tends to dominate, but tall lifters with long legs benefit from more leg frequency
You should only share a program once you have the experience to know what you are talking about
Body and soul must match and evolve together; a true warrior has both spirit and body
Bodybuilding does not have blocks, so a 12-week program duration is irrelevant
5x8-10 on dumbbell bench is too narrow a range; 4 sets of 8-12 is better
Three dumbbell bench variations back to back is too much; do dumbbell bench as strength work for 4x4-8, then rotate incline or floor press for 4x8-12
Standing dumbbell press is more athletic and works the core more than seated
Replace tricep kickbacks with behind-the-head extensions for long-head work, supersetted with lateral raises, because pressing days already cover the other heads
Keep goblet squats in higher rep ranges (8-12) because they challenge staying upright and thoracic extension
Rotate lunges and frog squats week to week rather than doing both after squats and stiff-leg deadlifts
Calf raises for 4x20 is an excellent set and rep selection
Novices tend to row with their arms, so keep dumbbell rows at lighter weights and 8-12 reps
Supersetting two row variations with different grips costs surprisingly little strength; grip is the only limit
Pullovers are godlike for the lats
Supinated rows are too dangerous for the biceps of novices; drop them
Three sets pair best with 12-15 reps, four sets with 10-15
Finish with pullovers and stand straight up to curl the same dumbbell with both hands
The upper back can take a lot of punishment and high volume
Dumbbell squats are inferior to barbell and goblet squats because of range of motion; they become a reverse dumbbell deadlift
Dumbbell squats and deadlifts on the same day are fine because the loads are too low to be detrimental
Dumbbell side bends are not very good; do side knee raises instead
Do not run the five days consecutively; spread them across a 7-8 day window with rest days
Pinwheel curls are underrated; do 4 sets for more direct forearm work
Do shrugs for 4x15-20; the traps will not be fried by it
Long-head triceps work is routinely neglected in programs
